content:
Emily (support): FYI, escalation from customer #3421 — streaming responses via our hosted API are getting cut off after ~15s then client reconnects see partial duplicate tokens. Happens only when request goes through ALB -> nginx sidecar -> Cloudflare. Customer repro steps + logs attached.
Alex Chen: thanks. can you paste the curl they used? also which model/route and whether this happens with both text-stream and chat-stream endpoints?
Emily (support): curl they ran (redacted auth):

```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  'https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=rwd-xx'
```
Requests stream OK for ~15s then connection closes with TCP FIN from client side. App logs show final tokens not received by client. Customer says when they hit backend directly (bypass ALB) stream completes fine.
Sophia Patel: sounds like some intermediate is buffering or hitting idle timeout and force-closing. ALB default idle timeout is 60s but that would close later. Could be nginx proxy_buffering or Cloudflare response buffering/clamping. Any nginx configs on the sidecar?

Emily (support): sidecar is the standard kube ingress-nginx with default upstream config. I asked for sidecar config dump and they sent:

```
proxy_buffers 8 16k;
proxy_buffer_size 8k;
proxy_read_timeout 60;
proxy_send_timeout 60;
proxy_http_version 1.1;
```
Alex Chen: proxy_read_timeout 60 matches ALB idle timeout if ALB is 60 -> but they said closes at 15s. That hints at Cloudflare or client or some middleware dropping smaller-ish idle writes when there are many small chunks. Also check if runtime is flushing after each chunk. Some frameworks buffer until a newline or buffer size reached.
Sophia Patel: exactly — our runtime sends tokens frequently but sometimes we only flush every N tokens depending on flush strategy. If nginx sees many tiny writes it may coalesce then hit some threshold and then connection gets torn down if no progress. Can we see app logs with token flush markers?

Emily (support): customer shared snippet from their client code (JS EventSource):

```
const es = new EventSource(url, { withCredentials: true });
es.onmessage = e => { console.log('tok', e.data); };
```
They also tried a raw curl --no-buffer and saw same problem.
Michael R: two quick checks: 1) confirm Transfer-Encoding: chunked is present on response; 2) check if intermediate sets Content-Length (that would break streaming). Also Cloudflare by default buffers responses from origin for HTML/JS if Enable: 'Response Buffering' turned on in some settings.

Alex Chen: I pulled our proxy logs (ingress-nginx) for the session:

```
2026-03-06T14:11:22Z ingress-nginx 10.0.1.5 GET /v1/stream 200 "upstream response body sent" 15.3s
2026-03-06T14:11:37Z kube-proxy connection closed by peer
```
Looks like ~15s then closed. Could be health probe or sidecar L7 idle detection. Any Envoy or service-mesh in path?

Emily (support): no envoy. Cloudflare in front of ALB (screenshot shows DNS proxied). Customer tried setting page rule to bypass cache and still hit same result.
Sophia Patel: here's a checklist to diagnose and fix — share with customer:
1) Run a direct curl against origin (bypass Cloudflare + ALB) — already done and it completes.
2) Try curl through ALB but bypass nginx sidecar (if possible) to narrow to nginx vs ALB.
3) On nginx, set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection "";` and `chunked_transfer_encoding on;` and restart; test.
4) On runtime, ensure explicit flush after each token: in Node/Express for SSE use `res.write("data: ...\n\n"); res.flush();` and ensure `compression` middleware is disabled for that route.
5) If Cloudflare in front, temporarily enable "Development Mode" or an origin bypass host to see if Cloudflare buffering causes it.

Alex Chen: add to that: check ALB idle timeout — if it's lower than expected it will close connection during slow token emission. default is 60s but they saw 15s, so maybe a custom rule or app-level keepalive misconfigured. Also check TCP keepalive and NLB vs ALB differences — NLB operates at layer 4 and will not buffer chunks, ALB may.

Emily (support): I passed checklist to customer and they tried: toggling nginx `proxy_buffering off` made the stream complete reliably for 2/2 tests. When they reverted, failures returned. They also verified `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` present when proxy_buffering off.

Michael R: good repro. That confirms nginx buffering was coalescing/holding chunks and then some timeout upstream caused the connection to drop. We should ship a recommended config doc for streaming endpoints and consider changing our default sidecar config for streaming routes.

Alex Chen: proposed nginx snippet to add to our helm chart for streaming services:

```
location /v1/stream {
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_cache off;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection "";
  chunked_transfer_encoding on;
  proxy_send_timeout 300s;
  proxy_read_timeout 300s;
}
```
Also note: disable gzip for that location, e.g., `gzip off;`, otherwise gzip may buffer until complete.

Sophia Patel: runtime note for other teams: in Go handlers using `flusher, ok := w.(http.Flusher)` then `w.Write([]byte("data: ...\n\n"))` then `flusher.Flush()` per token; in Python/uvicorn/gunicorn push with `await response.write()` and ensure worker_class supports streaming.

Emily (support): customer asked about billing impact of reconnect + duplicate tokens. We told them duplicate tokens might be counted twice if they re-request parts; recommend idempotency tokens or client-side dedup by tracking token ids if you include id metadata in events.

Alex Chen: followup actions for us: 1) update streaming runbook with nginx/ALB/Cloudflare checklist (added); 2) add a console warning on routes that enable streaming about recommended ingress settings; 3) create an infra PR to default `proxy_buffering off` for our streaming kube ingress annotations.
deploy-bot: rolled out ingress annotation change to staging (canary 10%).
ingest-bot: support ticket #3421 status updated -> waiting on staging canary validation.

Michael R: note for triage — if a customer still sees truncation after proxy_buffering off, check: TLS termination differences, HTTP/2 -> HTTP/1.1 translation (ALB supports HTTP/2 from client to ALB, but ALB->backend uses HTTP/1.1; ensure `proxy_http_version 1.1` and `proxy_set_header Connection ""` to allow streaming), and any edge WAF products that may enforce buffering.

Emily (support): customer validated staging fix and reported streams stable. Marking escalation resolved but keeping runbook updates open.

Alex Chen: great. I'll create the infra PR and add an entry in the streaming troubleshooting KB summarizing the nginx + Cloudflare + ALB gotchas + example curl repro and exact steps we used.

Emily (support): thanks everyone — saving logs + repro to the ticket and closing after infra PR merges. :thumbsup:
